Dispatch packet — Arc 19 build session

**Role:** MAJOR_PLINY for the the-stoa Arc 19 engagement.
**Directive:** substrate/arcs/arc-19-build-directive.md (committed at 6992b16; on origin/main).

**Your one job:** make the-stoa cold-cloneable. Add the entry-point skill set so a fresh user who clones the repo and opens it in Claude Code gets a guided first encounter (visual tour or guided install).

**Read first:**
1. substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md (your role file)
2. substrate/arcs/arc-19-build-directive.md (the work spec — full details on all 5 deliverables, Phase A locks, smoke test, ship beat)

**Comms:** POLYBIUS is polling this ticket. Surface questions via 'bw comment stoa--t3k <text>' and wait. Use positional comment text — no -m flag (Arc 16.1 §6.1 discipline). Otherwise execute autonomously per the directive.

**Phase A locks** (settled pre-dispatch — do NOT re-surface):
- File structure: SKILL.md + CLAUDE.md at root, skills/stoa-intro/ + skills/install-stoa/, README modify in place, LICENSE already shipped
- Skill names: stoa-intro (tour), install-stoa (install)
- Pitch Desktop hard, graceful degradation to text for CLI users
- License: MIT (LICENSE file at root); README license section needs update
- Out of scope: Stoa app, role files, case study, KG, cross-repo work

**Ship beat:** clean PASS smoke → autonomous commit + push to origin/main per u--7yg.11. Surface back here with commit sha + close ticket.

POLYBIUS

PLINY surface — verify-then-execute trigger before Phase A starts.

Activated, role/intent confirmed (MAJOR_PLINY, Arc 19 entry-point skills). Beginning recon turned up one structural contradiction with the directive that needs adjudication before I author skill 4:

**The standalone KG HTML is not on origin/main.** The directive (Phase B §2 line 241) treats 'design/Stoa_architecture/Stoa Architecture KG _standalone_.html' as a cross-reference that resolves on the cold clone. But:
- 'git ls-files design/' returns empty (entire design/ tree untracked)
- 'git log --all --diff-filter=A' for that path returns empty (never committed on any branch)
- No .gitignore exists in the repo (so it's not intentionally ignored — just never staged)
- File exists locally (1.7MB, mtime May 3) — only on this dev box

skills/stoa-intro/SKILL.md hangs entirely on serving that HTML via Chrome MCP. On a freshly-cloned the-stoa, the tour will 404 — which directly contradicts Arc 19's premise of cold-cloneability.

I see four options; flagging structural choice to you rather than picking silently:

(a) **Commit design/ as part of Arc 19 ship.** Cleanest — the directive's reference paths actually resolve. Adds ~all of design/ (HTML + assets + screenshots) to the Arc 19 diff. Total size unknown until I check; standalone HTML alone is 1.7MB.

(b) **Commit ONLY the standalone HTML (and any runtime assets it loads inline) in a separate prep commit before Arc 19.** Keeps the Arc 19 commit narrow to skills/README/CLAUDE.md.

(c) **Redesign stoa-intro to instruct the user to fetch the HTML separately** (e.g., from a release artifact or a sibling repo). Requires defining where 'separately' is. Ugly for a 'cold clone and go' story.

(d) **Something I'm not seeing** — e.g., design/ is intentionally a working dir, the HTML is regenerable from app/ source via a build step, etc.

My read: (a) is the right call given Arc 19's stated goal — the file is small enough and the alternative is the tour skill being broken-on-arrival. But this changes commit scope, so I want your call before proceeding.

Standing by; will set up a 5-min polling cron and wait. Other 4 deliverables can be authored in parallel while we settle this — they don't touch the standalone HTML — so I'll start on README + LICENSE-section + root SKILL.md + root CLAUDE.md + install-stoa skill while waiting for your call on the design/ question.

PLINY status — deliverables authored, blocked on design/ adjudication for ship.

Progress while waiting on your design/ call:
- README.md: 'Getting started' section prepended; License section updated to MIT framing (deliverable 1, done)
- SKILL.md (root, the-stoa-about): 30-sec pitch + 3-way branch + Desktop pitch + must-not list (deliverable 2, done)
- CLAUDE.md (root): web-search rule verbatim + repo-what-this-is + exploring/editing branches + authorship attribution (deliverable 3, done)
- skills/install-stoa/SKILL.md: 8 procedure beats + dry-run-first discipline + must-not list (deliverable 4, done)
- skills/stoa-intro/SKILL.md: 9 procedure beats + text fallback + Desktop pitch + must-not list (deliverable 5, authored speculatively against options a/b — same skill body either way; first beats need revision if you pick c or d)

Refined recommendation now that I've inventoried design/:
- design/ total = 3.4 MB
- design/Stoa_architecture/Stoa Architecture KG _standalone_.html = 1.7 MB (the load-bearing artifact for the tour)
- design/Stoa_architecture/screenshots/ = ~190 KB (5 PNGs documenting the modes — useful as text-fallback companion)
- design/Stoa_architecture/{app.jsx,kg-renderer.jsx,tweaks-panel.jsx,data.js,styles.css} = ~120 KB (Claude Design source the standalone is built from — not strictly needed at runtime)
- design/Stoa_architecture/uploads/{2 large pasted PNGs} = ~1.1 MB (working-session pasted screenshots — almost certainly not load-bearing)
- design/Stoa_case_study/ = 137 KB (separate Claude Design output — case-study HTML render + assets)

Cleanest narrow option I see — call it (b-narrow) — is committing JUST these for Arc 19's cold-clone integrity:
- design/Stoa_architecture/Stoa Architecture KG _standalone_.html (1.7 MB; what the tour serves)
- design/Stoa_architecture/screenshots/*.png (~190 KB; what the text fallback can reference)

Total ~1.9 MB added to the Arc 19 commit. The Claude Design source files and the working-session pasted PNGs are forkable separately if/when you want them in git, but they are NOT load-bearing for the tour. The Stoa_case_study/ HTML render is its own separate concern (case study lives at docs/case-study/case-study.md as the canonical text; the Claude Design HTML is a redundant render).

Standing by. Setting up surface-and-wait 5-min polling cron next per §6.2 — will cancel the moment you respond. Smoke test + ship are blocked on this call (smoke test §2 cross-reference list includes the standalone HTML; until design/ is resolved, smoke can't pass).
